2: // Auto-generated by `entire enable --agent opencode`

4: // Requires Bun runtime (used by OpenCode's plugin system for loading ESM plugins).
5: import type { Plugin } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"
6: 
7: export const EntirePlugin: Plugin = async ({ $, directory }) => {
8:   const ENTIRE_CMD = "entire"
9:   // Track seen user messages to fire turn-start only once per message
10:   const seenUserMessages = new Set<string>()
11:   // Track current session ID for message events (which don't include sessionID)
12:   let currentSessionID: string | null = null
13:   // In-memory store for message metadata (role, tokens, etc.)
14:   const messageStore = new Map<string, any>()
15: 
16:   /**
17:    * Pipe JSON payload to an entire hooks command (async).
18:    * Errors are logged but never thrown — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode.
19:    */
20:   async function callHook(hookName: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>) {
21:     try {
22:       const json = JSON.stringify(payload)
23:       await $`echo ${json} | ${ENTIRE_CMD} hooks opencode ${hookName}`.quiet().nothrow()
24:     } catch {
25:       // Silently ignore — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode
26:     }
27:   }
28: 
29:   /**
30:    * Synchronous variant for hooks that fire near process exit (turn-end, session-end).
31:    * `opencode run` breaks its event loop on the same session.status idle event that
32:    * triggers turn-end. The async callHook would be killed before completing.
33:    * Bun.spawnSync blocks the event loop, preventing exit until the hook finishes.
34:    */
35:   function callHookSync(hookName: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>) {
36:     try {
37:       const json = JSON.stringify(payload)
38:       Bun.spawnSync(["sh", "-c", `${ENTIRE_CMD} hooks opencode ${hookName}`], {
39:         cwd: directory,
40:         stdin: new TextEncoder().encode(json + "\n"),
41:         stdout: "ignore",
42:         stderr: "ignore",
43:       })
44:     } catch {
45:       // Silently ignore — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode
46:     }
47:   }
48: 
49:   return {
50:     event: async ({ event }) => {
51:       switch (event.type) {
52:         case "session.created": {
53:           const session = (event as any).properties?.info
54:           if (!session?.id) break
55:           // Reset per-session tracking state when switching sessions.
56:           if (currentSessionID !== session.id) {
57:             seenUserMessages.clear()
58:             messageStore.clear()
59:           }
60:           currentSessionID = session.id
61:           await callHook("session-start", {
62:             session_id: session.id,
63:           })
64:           break
65:         }
66: 
67:         case "message.updated": {
68:           const msg = (event as any).properties?.info
69:           if (!msg) break
70:           // Store message metadata (role, time, tokens, etc.)
71:           messageStore.set(msg.id, msg)
72:           break
73:         }
74: 
75:         case "message.part.updated": {
76:           const part = (event as any).properties?.part
77:           if (!part?.messageID) break
78: 
79:           // Fire turn-start on the first text part of a new user message
80:           const msg = messageStore.get(part.messageID)
81:           if (msg?.role === "user" && part.type === "text" && !seenUserMessages.has(msg.id)) {
82:             seenUserMessages.add(msg.id)
83:             const sessionID = msg.sessionID ?? currentSessionID
84:             if (sessionID) {
85:               await callHook("turn-start", {
86:                 session_id: sessionID,
87:                 prompt: part.text ?? "",
88:               })
89:             }
90:           }
91:           break
92:         }
93: 
94:         case "session.status": {
95:           // session.status fires in both TUI and non-interactive (run) mode.
96:           // session.idle is deprecated and not reliably emitted in run mode.
97:           const props = (event as any).properties
98:           if (props?.status?.type !== "idle") break
99:           const sessionID = props?.sessionID
100:           if (!sessionID) break
101:           // Use sync variant: `opencode run` exits on the same idle event,
102:           // so an async hook would be killed before completing.
103:           callHookSync("turn-end", {
104:             session_id: sessionID,
105:           })
106:           break
107:         }
108: 
109:         case "session.compacted": {
110:           const sessionID = (event as any).properties?.sessionID
111:           if (!sessionID) break
112:           await callHook("compaction", {
113:             session_id: sessionID,
114:           })
115:           break
116:         }
117: 
118:         case "session.deleted": {
119:           const session = (event as any).properties?.info
120:           if (!session?.id) break
121:           seenUserMessages.clear()
122:           messageStore.clear()
123:           currentSessionID = null
124:           // Use sync variant: session-end may fire during shutdown.
125:           callHookSync("session-end", {
126:             session_id: session.id,
127:           })
128:           break
129:         }
130:       }
131:     },
132:   }

# OpenCode (preview)

> Integrate Entire with OpenCode for AI coding session capture

OpenCode is an AI-powered terminal coding agent. Entire integrates with OpenCode via its plugin system, automatically capturing sessions and checkpoints. The OpenCode integration is in preview and may contain bugs.

## Prerequisites

* [Entire CLI installed](/cli/installation)
* [OpenCode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) installed
* A Git repository with Entire enabled

## How It Works

Entire integrates with OpenCode through a TypeScript plugin that hooks into OpenCode's event system. When you enable Entire with the OpenCode agent, the plugin is installed automatically:

```bash  theme={null}
entire enable --agent opencode
```

The plugin communicates with Entire via hooks:

1. **Session Detection** - The plugin fires on `session.created` events
2. **Turn Tracking** - Each user prompt triggers `turn-start`; when the agent goes idle, `turn-end` fires
3. **Transcript Export** - On `turn-end`, Entire calls `opencode export` to capture the full transcript
4. **Checkpoint Creation** - Checkpoints are created based on your strategy
5. **Session Storage** - Data saved to the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch

### Captured Data

| Data         | Description                                     |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Conversation | Full transcript of prompts and responses        |
| File changes | Files modified via edit, write, and patch tools |
| Tool calls   | Tool invocations with inputs and outputs        |
| Token usage  | Input, output, reasoning, and cache tokens      |
| Timestamps   | Session, message, and checkpoint timing         |

## Features

### Rewind Support

Rewind to previous checkpoints during or after a session:

```bash  theme={null}
# Interactive mode
entire rewind

# Or rewind to a specific checkpoint
entire rewind --to <checkpoint-id>

# List available rewind points
entire rewind --list
```

| Flag            | Description                                       |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `--to <commit>` | Rewind to specific commit ID (non-interactive)    |
| `--list`        | List available rewind points (JSON output)        |
| `--logs-only`   | Only restore logs, don't modify working directory |
| `--reset`       | Reset branch to commit (destructive)              |

When you rewind, Entire reimports the checkpoint-state transcript into OpenCode's database so you can continue seamlessly.

### Resume Previous Sessions

Resume a previous OpenCode session by switching to its branch:

```bash  theme={null}
entire resume <branch>
```

This command:

1. Checks out the specified branch
2. Finds the session ID from commits unique to this branch
3. Restores the session log if it doesn't exist locally
4. Shows the command to resume the session (e.g., `opencode -s <session-id>`)

| Flag          | Description                                       |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `-f, --force` | Resume from older checkpoint without confirmation |

### Explain Commits

View or generate explanations of how code was written:

```bash  theme={null}
# Explain a specific commit
entire explain --commit abc1234

# Explain a specific checkpoint
entire explain --checkpoint a3b2c4d5

# Show full transcript
entire explain --full
```

| Flag                    | Description                                         |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `-c, --checkpoint <id>` | Explain a specific checkpoint (ID or prefix)        |
| `--commit <sha>`        | Explain a specific commit (SHA or ref)              |
| `--full`                | Show full parsed transcript (all prompts/responses) |
| `-s, --short`           | Show summary only (omit prompts and files)          |

### Mid-Turn Commits

When OpenCode commits during a turn (before the turn ends), Entire captures a checkpoint for that commit. The transcript is fetched on-demand via `opencode export` so the checkpoint includes the latest agent activity.

## Best Practices

### Use Manual Commit Strategy

For terminal AI tools like OpenCode:

```bash  theme={null}
entire enable --agent opencode --strategy manual-commit
```

Commit when you've made meaningful progress:

```bash  theme={null}
git add .
git commit -m "Implement feature with OpenCode"
```

## Example Workflow

```bash  theme={null}
# 1. Enable Entire with OpenCode
cd my-project
entire enable --agent opencode

# 2. Start OpenCode
opencode

# 3. Work with OpenCode
# Ask it to write code, make changes, etc.

# 4. Rewind if needed
entire rewind

# 5. Commit when ready
git add .
git commit -m "Add feature with OpenCode"

# 6. Push to see on entire.io
git push
```

Your session is now visible on [entire.io](https://entire.io) with full context for code review.

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Session not detected">
    1. Ensure you're in an Entire-enabled repo: `entire status`
    2. Verify OpenCode is running from within the repository
    3. Check that the plugin is installed: look for the Entire plugin in your OpenCode config
    4. Check Git hooks are installed: `ls .git/hooks`
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="No checkpoints created">
    1. Checkpoints require file changes — ensure OpenCode is modifying files
    2. Check your strategy settings in `.entire/settings.json`
    3. Verify `opencode export` works: `opencode export <session-id>`
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Transcript not captured">
    1. The plugin calls `opencode export` to fetch transcripts — ensure this command works
    2. Check that the `.opencode` directory exists in your repository
    3. Look for errors in the Entire hook output: run `entire hooks opencode turn-end` manually
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

## Limitations

* The integration is in preview and may have rough edges
* Plugin requires Bun runtime (used by OpenCode's plugin system)
* Session detection relies on OpenCode's event system
* Works best with the manual-commit strategy

parts.text:
Boa, conferi e faz sentido a sua dúvida.

O que está **global** é só o binário (`brew install entire`).  
O que faz o Entire “rodar” é **por repositório** quando você executa `entire enable` dentro dele.

No seu caso, no `mapctx` ele está ativo porque existem artefatos locais:
- plugin local do OpenCode: `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts:1`
- config local do Entire: `.entire/settings.json`
- hooks git locais chamando `entire hooks ...`: `.git/hooks/pre-push:1`, `.git/hooks/post-commit:1`, `.git/hooks/prepare-commit-msg:1`, `.git/hooks/commit-msg:1`

E eu validei em outros repos (`br-acc`, `opencode-plus`): `entire status` deu `not set up`.

Então: sua expectativa está correta — ele deveria funcionar só onde você habilitou.  
Se parecer “global”, geralmente é porque o comando existe no PATH global, mas sem `enable` no repo ele não captura sessão.

Se quiser, no próximo passo eu te passo um checklist rápido para auditar qualquer repo em 10s (pra confirmar se está enabled ou não).
